body: Seeded randomness — a run's randomness from one seed; two runs of one seed read the same state (v030-13).

Capability `matrix#v030-13` (escher-0.3.0): requirement «A run's randomness comes from a seed, so two runs of one seed
read the same state»; observed gap «Randomness depends on the host.»; method `integration`; acceptance «Two runs given
one seed read the same state at every step.» Intent §Findings 9 (C2): «A run's randomness comes from a seed, and its
fonts are bundled, so two hosts read the same state the same way. These are the trust layer under E2's replays.»

- A seed for a run: a run of the driver (a held `Session`, and the harness it holds) is given one seed, and every
  source of randomness the run's app and page can read draws from it — so two runs given one seed read the same state
  at every step, and a kept check replays the run it recorded.

- The app-facing source: a Dioxus app hosted by the driver reads its randomness from the run's seed, through one
  engine-provided source, rather than from the host.
- The page-facing source: a page script's `Math.random` in a seeded run draws from the run's seed.

- The proof: an integration check, both layout modes, of two runs given one seed reading the same state (snapshot text
  and diffs) at every step of a scripted sequence on an app that reads randomness, and of two runs given different
  seeds reading a difference — so the check cannot pass vacuously.

- Not bundled fonts (v030-14, the next entry), not start-in-a-state (v030-08), not auto-exploration (v030-09) —
  auto-exploration and replay are this seed's later readers, not this chunk's work.

- No new listener, port, socket, env read or log field carrying a seed's value; a seed is not a secret, but it stays
  out of every log line by the content rule unless a ratified decision says otherwise.
- The windowed shell (`blitz-shell`) and the browser app are not seeded runs.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-11-14-seeded-randomness · **Version:** escher-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-11-14T02:22:10Z

A run's randomness comes from one seed, so two runs given one seed read the same state at every step (`matrix#v030-13`,
intent §Findings 9, C2). Today no randomness source is offered to an app: a Dioxus app that wants a random number takes
it from the host. This chunk adds the one engine-provided source a Dioxus app reads — `dioxus_native_dom::SeededRandom`
through the hook `use_seeded_random` — and makes every harness-built Dioxus document read one run seed: a fixed
`DEFAULT_SEED` unless the builder of its `VirtualDom` provides another at the root. Every driver session (command line,
host, `mcp` and coverage roles, replay) boots through `Harness::from_vdom`, so every hosted run reads the default seed
and every kept check replays the run it recorded.

The shape follows the precedents the history files name: a run input reaching the app as a root context
(`stand_root`'s `TimerTicks`; the ungated `reached` record, `(architecture · decision/dioxus-root-contexts)`), and the
harness supplying determinism to every document it builds as it supplies the one `VirtualClock`
`(architecture · decision/one-virtual-clock)`. The module is ungated, like `reached` and `signal_registry`
`(architecture · decision/accessibility-feature-gating)`, so the wasm build compiles it. It is written by hand
(splitmix64), taking no dependency `(security-plan · decision/workspace-inherited-dependency-versions)`, and adds no
log site, span, field, print or env read `(obs-plan · decision/driver-spans-carry-no-content)`,
`(security-plan · decision/driver-reads-only-rust-log)`.

No seed crosses a driver carrier in this chunk: whether `start` takes a `seed` is the founder's fork F1
(`.andromeda/runs/2026-11-14T01-51-56-phase/founder-forks.md`), a Boundary widening (`rul-izni57qv`), and the plan is
built on its lean A — the run's seed is the boot's — on the operator's directive that the founder's forks are listed
with their lean and not waited on (`inputs#I1`). The page-facing `Math.random` is outside every driver run and outside
this chunk (scope, premise-corrected). The proof is a new stand check over a fixture app that reads the seeded source:
two runs of one seed equal at every step in both layout modes and in a second process, two seeds differing, and a kept
check replaying its seeded run.

1. **The seeded source** — create `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/seed.rs` (opens with `//!` naming what it is and that
   it holds no content and logs nothing; keeps arch S4). It holds:
   - `pub const DEFAULT_SEED: u64 = 0` — the seed a harness-built document reads when its builder gives none.
   - `pub struct SeededRandom` — `Clone`; every clone shares ONE generator state (an `Rc<Cell<u64>>`), so every
     component of a document draws from one stream in the order the draws happen. A hand `Debug` writes the type
     name alone, no state (obs S4).
   - `SeededRandom::from_seed(seed: u64) -> Self`; `next_u64(&self) -> u64` — splitmix64 (state advanced by
     `0x9E3779B97F4A7C15`, then the two xor-shift-multiply rounds `0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9`, `0x94D049BB133111EB`, all
     wrapping); `below(&self, bound: u64) -> u64` — a value in `0..bound` by the 128-bit multiply-high of `next_u64`
     and `bound`, `0` for a `bound` of `0` (no panic path, no division).
   - `pub fn use_seeded_random() -> SeededRandom` — a Dioxus hook: `use_hook` once per call site, returning the
     `SeededRandom` the nearest ancestor (the root) provides through dioxus-core's context lookup
     (`try_consume_context`), else a generator seeded from the host (a private `from_host` taking std's
     `RandomState` hasher output — std only), which is the windowed shell's case, not a run.
   - An inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`: splitmix64's published first three outputs for seed 0
     (`0xE220A8397B1DCDAF`, `0x6E789E6AA1B965F4`, `0x06C45D188009454F`) as a stated table with its row count asserted;
     two generators of one seed equal over 1,000 draws, two seeds differing at the first draw; a clone advancing the
     shared stream; `below` inside its bound over a stated table of bounds (`1`, `6`, `u64::MAX`) and `0` for bound
     `0`. Failures name a row index only (keeps tests S5).

2. **Export it, ungated** — in `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/lib.rs`, `mod seed;` beside `reached` and
   `signal_registry` with no `cfg(feature = "accessibility")`, and `pub use seed::{DEFAULT_SEED, SeededRandom,
   use_seeded_random};`.

3. **The harness's run seed** — in `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/harness.rs`, `Harness::from_vdom` reads, before
   `DioxusDocument::new`, whether the vdom's root scope already holds a `SeededRandom` context (dioxus-core's root
   context lookup inside `VirtualDom::in_runtime`); where it holds none, it provides
   `SeededRandom::from_seed(DEFAULT_SEED)` with `VirtualDom::provide_root_context`. A root context the builder provided
   (`VirtualDom::with_root_context(SeededRandom::from_seed(s))`) stands. `from_vdom`'s `///` states it;
   `from_component` reaches it through `from_vdom`; `wrap` provides nothing (a wrapped document keeps what its builder
   gave, as it keeps its clock). `HarnessOptions` is unchanged. The harness adds no `tracing`, no print and no env read
   `(security-plan · decision/test-harness-no-tracing-no-style)`.

4. **The proof** — create `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_seeded_randomness.rs`, opening with `//!` naming the
   behaviour (keeps arch S1, tests S1; its `stand_` prefix puts it in the stand-repeat rounds by the leg's glob, tests
   S7). Its fixture, stated in the file (one reader, tests S6): a component reading `use_seeded_random`, drawing three
   die values (`below(6) + 1`) at its first render and one more on each click of a keyed `button` `id="roll"`, each
   value a keyed list item whose text is the value; every actionable element keyed (layouts S1). Each run boots it with
   `Harness::from_vdom(…, seven_guis::stand::options(incremental))` — the stand's pinned viewport and bundled font,
   offline — held in a `Session::start`, and is driven through `Session::run` alone: a `snapshot`, then five `click`s
   on `roll`, each followed by a `snapshot`; a run's reading is its eleven answer lines in order. Every test runs both
   layout modes (keeps tests S2), takes no sleep and reads no wall clock (tests S3), prints nothing but the re-run
   child's digests (obs S1), and its failures name a mode and a step index, never an answer (tests S5). Tests:
   - `the_fixture_reads_the_seeded_source` — fixture-first: under seed 7 and seed 8 the boot snapshot texts differ
     (keeps arch S3).
   - `one_seed_two_runs_read_the_same_state_at_every_step` — two runs given seed 7: all eleven answer lines equal,
     step by step.
   - `two_seeds_read_different_states` — runs given seed 7 and seed 8: the boot answer line differs (the vacuity
     control of the test above).
   - `a_run_given_no_seed_reads_the_default_seed` — a run whose vdom carries no `SeededRandom` reads, step by step,
     the same eleven lines as a run given `SeededRandom::from_seed(DEFAULT_SEED)`.
   - `a_second_process_reads_the_same_state` — the re-execution pattern of `stand_id_persistence`: the test re-runs
     its own binary with a fixed argv naming one child test, which prints, one per line, `escher_driver::answer_digest`
     of each of a seed-7 run's eleven answer lines (digests only, no answer text); the parent reads them and asserts
     them equal to its own run's digests (both layout modes). Its child streams are read, not inherited (tests S4).
   - `a_kept_check_replays_its_seeded_run` (`cfg(unix)`, item by item, `(test-plan · decision/recording-checks-unix-gated)`)
     — a seed-7 session recording into an owner-only directory under `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` (the build-time path the
     session checks already read), its kept check read back with `Check::from_bytes`, then `Check::replay` on a fresh
     seed-7 session reads every step equal, and on a fresh seed-8 session stops at its first step; the directory is
     removed after.

5. **Lean A held** — no file under `packages/escher-driver/`, `examples/seven_guis/` or `tests/blitz-tests/checks/`
   changes, and `Cargo.lock` does not move (no dependency): no verb, argument kind, carrier, kept-check key, span field
   or exit is added `(architecture · decision/validated-verb-set-widened-by-ratification)`,
   `(security-plan · decision/closed-driver-verb-schema)`. The stand reads no randomness, so every served task and both
   committed Counter checks read as before under the default seed.

6. **Gates** — run the `[[gate]]` entries in order; `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast` last before the operator
   pass. The red-before-green control of the new check is implement's one-shot run, never an entry: with step 3's
   provide removed and the fixture booted with no seed, `a_run_given_no_seed_reads_the_default_seed` reads red
   (`gate.py control`, the file `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/harness.rs` and the provide line it removes); with
   `below` returning a constant, `the_fixture_reads_the_seeded_source` reads red (the file
   `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/seed.rs`).
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/seed.rs` — `DEFAULT_SEED`, `SeededRandom`, `use_seeded_random`, its unit tests
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_seeded_randomness.rs` — the proof over a seeded fixture, both layout modes
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/lib.rs` — `mod seed;` ungated and its three re-exports
- `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/harness.rs` — `Harness::from_vdom` provides the default run seed where the vdom holds none

- `packages/blitz-test-harness/Cargo.toml` — named by research as a possible edit; the harness already declares `dioxus-core` and `dioxus-native-dom`, so implement leaves it unchanged unless the build names a missing dependency

The gates run on the dev host, Linux. Nothing boots outside the harness: there is no live leg, and the real boot is
/implement P3's. The base sha in the census entries is HEAD as this plan is written,
`4f68f0d523aed2d6c3ef7e34ddccf2ca05c0506c`.

The diff is OS-sensitive: the new check re-executes its own binary (a process) and gates its recording test on
`cfg(unix)`. So the plan carries the operator's hygiene, push and CI-read entries: CI's «Test (windows)» and «Test

   behaviour (keeps arch S1, tests S1; its `stand_` prefix puts it in the stand-repeat rounds by the leg's glob, tests
   S7). Its fixture, stated in the file (one reader, tests S6): a component reading `use_seeded_random`, drawing three
   die values (`below(6) + 1`) at its first render and one more on each click of a keyed `button` `id="roll"`, each
   value a keyed list item whose text is the value; every actionable element keyed (layouts S1). Each run boots it with
   `Harness::from_vdom(…, seven_guis::stand::options(incremental))` — the stand's pinned viewport and bundled font,
   offline — held in a `Session::start`, and is driven through `Session::run` alone: a `snapshot`, then five `click`s
   on `roll`, each followed by a `snapshot`; a run's reading is its eleven answer lines in order. Every test runs both
   layout modes (keeps tests S2), takes no sleep and reads no wall clock (tests S3), prints nothing but the re-run
   child's digests (obs S1), and its failures name a mode and a step index, never an answer (tests S5). Tests:
   - `the_fixture_reads_the_seeded_source` — fixture-first: under seed 7 and seed 8 the boot snapshot texts differ
     (keeps arch S3).
   - `one_seed_two_runs_read_the_same_state_at_every_step` — two runs given seed 7: all eleven answer lines equal,
     step by step.
   - `two_seeds_read_different_states` — runs given seed 7 and seed 8: the boot answer line differs (the vacuity
     control of the test above).
   - `a_run_given_no_seed_reads_the_default_seed` — a run whose vdom carries no `SeededRandom` reads, step by step,
     the same eleven lines as a run given `SeededRandom::from_seed(DEFAULT_SEED)`.
   - `a_second_process_reads_the_same_state` — the re-execution pattern of `stand_id_persistence`: the test re-runs
     its own binary (`std::env::current_exe()`) once with the fixed argv `--ignored --exact {the child} --nocapture`,
     setting or removing no env var, its output captured by `Command::output` (which reaps the child); the child, an
     `#[ignore]` test of the same file, prints, one per line, `escher_driver::answer_digest`
     of each of a seed-7 run's eleven answer lines (digests only, no answer text); the parent reads them and asserts
     them equal to its own run's digests (both layout modes). Its child streams are read, not inherited (tests S4).
   - `a_kept_check_replays_its_seeded_run` (`cfg(unix)`, item by item, `(test-plan · decision/recording-checks-unix-gated)`)
     — a seed-7 session recording into an owner-only directory under `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` (the build-time path the
     session checks already read), its kept check read back with `Check::from_bytes`, then `Check::replay` on a fresh
     seed-7 session reads every step equal, and on a fresh seed-8 session stops at its first step; the directory is
     removed after.

body:
## 2026-11-14-seeded-randomness — Standard Contracts: 1 row(s)
**Section:** Standard Contracts
**Change:** + decision/no-seed-on-carriers — No seed crosses the driver's carriers
**Why:** decision/no-seed-on-carriers: Fork F1 was answered A, no seed on any carrier, provisional for the founder, and no row records the absence; the proposer's wording said every run reads the default seed, false for an in-process builder's root seed.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-14T07-12-40-wrap/

- Optional capabilities are Cargo features forwarded across crates (each dioxus-native feature forwards to the same-named blitz feature; `accessibility` also to dioxus-native-dom's, which gates its own `accessibility_tree` override and its `snapshot`, `snapshot_diff`, `snapshot_text`, `actionable` and `graph` modules, its `signal_registry`, `reached` and `seed` modules ungated, so an app registers state whatever its features and the reached record compiles on the wasm build that leaves `accessibility` off). The workspace takes both Dioxus crates with `default-features = false`, so a feature is on only where a crate names it or depends on a crate that names it — escher-driver names dioxus-native-dom's `accessibility`, which reaches both seven_guis binaries through that edge.

- `DioxusDocument` (`vdom`, `inner`, `initial_build`, `poll`, `handle_ui_event`, `vdom_state.try_element_to_node_id(ElementId)`), `NodeHandle` backing `MountedData`; under `accessibility`, the read-only UI graph `DioxusDocument::graph() -> UiGraph` (`UiGraph { nodes, states }`: one `GraphNode { id, owner, component, handlers, reads }` per snapshot node in pre-order, `GraphState { name, component, declared, writers, readers }`, `WriteFlag::{Undeclared, Unconfirmed}`), holding no `NodeId`; ungated, the graph registry `use_graph_state(name, writers, subscribers)` (`DeclaredWrite`, `SignalRegistry`), whose first hook provides a `SignalRegistry` context at `ScopeId::ROOT`; ungated too, the reached record (`DioxusDocument::record_reached`, `reached_handlers`, `ReachedHandler`), written only where it was switched on; ungated too, the run seed — `SeededRandom` (public, re-exported: a splitmix64 generator whose clones share one state, so every component of one document draws from one stream in draw order; `from_seed(u64)`, `next_u64`, `below(bound)` — the high bits of the 128-bit product, 0 for a bound of 0, no panic path; `Debug` writes the type name alone), `use_seeded_random` (the root's `SeededRandom` from a root context, else a generator seeded from the host's per-process random keys, the windowed shell's case outside any run) and `DEFAULT_SEED` (the `u64` seed 0), one seed held as a Dioxus root context so two runs of one seed read the same state at every step, in both layout modes and across processes (`stand_seeded_randomness`).

| Parallelism & misc | rayon 1, slotmap, rustc-hash, bytes, smallvec, thin-vec, atomic_refcell, bitflags, bytemuck, pollster, smol_str, thread_local; mimalloc, the global allocator of two upstream-only binaries, the browser app (by default) and the WPT runner; no PRNG crate (since 2026-11-14-seeded-randomness): seeded randomness's splitmix64 is written by hand and its host fallback seed comes from std `RandomState`, no package entering `Cargo.lock` |

The driver's core (unpublished, no `[features]` of its own, no binary): a **session** — one headless app instance held by one process while commands arrive — the **command and refusal schema**, the one definition of what can be asked of the driver and of how it says no, the **executor** that runs a call on the held instance, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli the **command line** that carries a call out of the process, and since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the **MCP server** that serves the fourteen verbs as MCP tools over a caller's reader and writer (the `escher-session mcp` role), and since 2026-10-12-self-description the **self-description** (`describe`) that `help` answers on both surfaces, and since 2026-10-19-session-recording the **recording**: a session whose launcher names a recording directory keeps its answered calls at rest as one owner-only replayable check (`std` only, unix only like the socket), and since 2026-10-19-visual-lint the **visual lint** (`Session::lint` in process and the `lint` verb, the eighth instance verb, on every carrier (the socket's `call`, the command line, an MCP tool, `help`'s listing) and recorded — built by «Visual lint» (its gated part)), which reads the held screen and returns its layout and contrast defects as typed findings, which cross on the ratified carriers and rest in a kept check as the `lint` verb's answer — stable ids, the closed defect words and numbers, no page text, colour, control value or `NodeId` (a ratified boundary widening), and since 2026-11-07-ui-graph the **UI graph** (the `graph` verb, the ninth instance verb, on every carrier and recorded), which reads the held screen's graph through `DioxusDocument::graph` and answers stable ids, owner ids, component names, registered state names, handler event names, the declared writes, the closed flag words `undeclared` and `unconfirmed` and booleans, never a value, typed text or `NodeId` (a ratified boundary widening), and since 2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here the **actions read** (`Session::actions` and the `actions` verb, the tenth instance verb, on every carrier and recorded), which lists each actionable node of the held screen with what each id-taking verb would answer now, answering stable ids, owner ids, the table's verb words, the closed cause words and `keyed` booleans, never a value, typed text or `NodeId` (a ratified boundary widening). It is app-agnostic: the caller supplies the boot and the time step, and the crate names no app and no stand type. `Session::run` validates a call, looks its target up on the screen, refuses a target that cannot take the action, runs its verb, settles the instance and returns a typed `Outcome` — for a call made in process, and for one a host decoded from its socket. A call and its answer cross the socket (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10), and an MCP client's stdio (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10, «Ратифицировать как есть»); since 2026-10-19-session-recording a recorded session's calls — the ids they named among them — rest in a kept check with its answers' digests and, since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay, each answer kept whole — its line as the driver wrote it, masked as on every carrier, a shot's without its pixels — so the screens' ids, names, values, snapshot text, diffs, a lint's findings, a UI graph's names, closed flag words and booleans, and an actions answer's ids, owner ids, verb words, closed cause words and booleans rest there too, never logged (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-19, F1 A · F2 B · F3 B); a kept check replays through `Session::run` alone (`Check::replay`), and since 2026-11-08-handler-coverage the **coverage reader** (`handler_coverage` and the command line's `coverage` role) replays kept checks, each on a fresh session, and lists the UI graph's handlers no check exercised, and the repository's own two scripted stand checks are committed in git, the one exception to owner-only. A settle verb on the socket is a later route entry. Since 2026-11-14-seeded-randomness no run seed crosses the driver's carriers — no verb, argument, command-line flag, MCP tool field, kept-check key or span field carries one — so every driver session and every kept check's replay reads the default seed; a seed reaches a run only from in-process code that builds its VirtualDom (provisional, the operator's answer A to the founder's fork).

- **`dioxus-native-dom`** — headless Dioxus renderer on blitz (`DioxusDocument`): stable element ids, the snapshot, its text, parts and diff, the UI graph, the reached record and the run's seeded randomness (`SeededRandom`, `use_seeded_random`, `DEFAULT_SEED`)

- **`blitz-test-harness`** — headless `Harness` for blitz documents: virtual time, the run seed (`from_vdom` provides `SeededRandom::from_seed(DEFAULT_SEED)` where the root holds none), pump, settle, input synthesis, inspection, screenshot, contrast

- Constructors pump once; `wrap` does not. The run seed (since 2026-11-14-seeded-randomness): `from_vdom` provides `SeededRandom::from_seed(DEFAULT_SEED)` as a root context where the vdom's root holds none, before the document is built, so every component draws from one stream; a `SeededRandom` the builder gave as a root context stands; `wrap` provides none. The harness's time (since 2026-10-18-one-virtual-clock, ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) is a `VirtualClock` its documents share: `HarnessOptions::into_config(self, &VirtualClock)` puts a clone in `DocumentConfig.clock`, so `from_html_with` and `from_vdom`, and through them `from_html` and `from_component`, build documents that read it, while `wrap(doc)` gives the harness a fresh `VirtualClock` and the wrapped document keeps the clock its own config gave it; `time()` reads that clock in seconds; `tick(dt)` advances it, a negative or non-finite `dt` moving nothing, and `advance_time(&mut self, by: Duration)` advances it by exactly `by`, each then pumping; `screenshot`, `screenshot_rect`, `text_contrast` and `settle` never move it. `pump` polls with no waker and resolves at harness time; `dispatch` / `dispatch_recorded` do not pump; input helpers pump after dispatch — `apple_keybinding(command)` among them, which dispatches `UiEvent::AppleStandardKeybinding` to the focused element as a macOS window does for a standard key binding (`deleteBackward:`); exercised on every OS since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness by `stand_keyboard::the_apple_delete_binding_deletes_on_every_os` (green on the linux, windows and macOS legs), and on the macOS CI leg by the driver's `press backspace` in `stand_act_keys` and, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli, by `stand_act_filled`'s clearing test (a `type` with an empty text deleting through the driver's own Backspace press) — and `scroll_into_view(node_id)`, which calls `BaseDocument::scroll_into_view` at once and by the least movement on each axis (every scrolling box that holds the node, then the viewport, a row of an open select list moving the list's `scroll_y` alone); it has no check of its own: the driver's `scroll` calls it, and `stand_actionable_keys` scrolls each Home card into view with it before a raw click. A raw `click` on an element lying outside the padding box of a box that clips it does not land on it; and for a box that is itself scrolled `layout_rect`, `layout_rect_of` and `center_of` read where the box stands — a box at (40, 50) reads (40, 50) at every scroll offset of its own, in both layout modes — as `BaseDocument::get_client_bounding_rect` and the snapshot's `bounds` do (built on `Node::absolute_position`; `scrolled_box_absolute_position` its check, ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18).

- Source reads no secret: env reads are `WPT_DIR`, `PAINT_TREE_BENCH_HTML`, `HOME`, `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, `RUST_LOG` (escher-telemetry's filter) and `MULTI_DOC_N` · `MULTI_DOC_SEQ` · `MULTI_DOC_FLAT` (the root example `multi_doc` alone) only — and, at build time in the session checks, `CARGO_BIN_EXE_escher-session` and `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` — plus `TMPDIR` through `std::env::temp_dir()` at two test-only sites, escher-driver's unix-only client unit test and blitz-vibey-script's `tests/dom.rs` helper `temp_dir_with_files` (test code only, not secret). The seeded source of randomness takes its seed only from in-process code (a root context the virtual DOM's builder gives, else the default seed 0; outside any run, the host's per-process random keys), reading no environment variable, file or carrier — keep it so. Never commit `.env*`.

- **In-process harness (measured):** `blitz-test-harness::Harness` — construct (`from_html`, `from_component`, `from_vdom` — which, before its one pump, provides `SeededRandom::from_seed(DEFAULT_SEED)` as a root context where the vdom's root holds none, a root context the builder gave standing; `HarnessOptions` also takes `font_ctx` and `incremental`), `pump`/`tick`/`advance_time` (the harness's time a `VirtualClock` its harness-built documents read — `tick(dt)` advancing it, a negative or non-finite `dt` moving nothing, `advance_time(Duration)` by exactly the duration, each then pumping; `screenshot`, `screenshot_rect`, `text_contrast` and `settle` never moving it; `wrap(doc)` keeping the clock the document's own config gave it; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), `settle` (that pass repeated until no work is due: `Settled`, or `NotSettled` naming the busy class — `Loads` at once when a request is in flight or a render-blocking resource is pending after a quiet pass, else `Render`, `Loads` or `Layout` read off the last pass at the 64-pass bound; no clock read but the harness's, no time advanced, no load waited on; the crate-private load counter forwarding `NetHandler::error` to the handler it wraps, so a failed stylesheet reaches the document, stops counting as a pending render-blocking resource and does not read `NotSettled { busy: Loads }`, and the driver's `settle_waiting` returns where it would otherwise have run to `LOAD_WAIT`), input helpers that pump, inspection (`query`, `layout_rect`, `text_content`, `focused`, `hit`, `dom_string`), and since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot a paint with no display — `screenshot` / `screenshot_rect` into `VelloCpuImageRenderer`, composited over opaque white, at the harness's own time with no tick or pump, a document with no font refused `FontsUnavailable`; and since 2026-10-13-stand-contrast-harness a contrast reader — `text_contrast(node_id) -> Option<TextContrast>`, reading and changing nothing (no mutation, input, pump or settle): the text-bearing element's computed `color`, font size and weight over the background composited source-over from its ancestors' `background-color`s onto the root-else-`body` canvas over opaque white, `None` with no text or where an element on the walk has `opacity` below 1, a filter, a background image or a `mix-blend-mode` other than `normal` (`paints_more_than_colour`, through `resolved_style_value`), `Session::lint`'s `contrast` reading the same with no second formula, and `contrast_ratio` the WCAG 2.x ratio. See `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`.

- Constructors `from_html`, `from_html_with(html, HarnessOptions)`, `from_component`, `from_vdom` pump once (`from_vdom` first providing `SeededRandom::from_seed(DEFAULT_SEED)` as a root context where the vdom's root holds none — a root context the builder gave stands); `wrap` does not.
